PROP
42
PROHIBITS NEW STATE PERSONAL PROPERTY TAXES AND CERTAIN RETROACTIVE STATE TAXES. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Prohibits any new state tax (1) imposed on the ownership of personal property (all things people own other than real estate), or (2) that applies retroactively based on taxpayer’s past activities. Nullifies taxes enacted after January 1, 2026 that conflict with this measure. Fiscal Impact: Possibility that tax revenues will not go up as much in the future. Supporters: CA Professional Firefighters; State Building & Construction Trades Council of CA; AMVETS Department of CA Opponents: US Senator Bernie Sanders; SEIU United Healthcare Workers West
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: The state could not establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: The state would continue to have the option to establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
California’s Constitution currently allows the Legislature to tax retirement and savings—even though you already paid taxes on that money when you earned it! Prop. 42 protects Californians from this double taxation, by prohibiting new and retroactive taxes on personal property, including retirement and savings. You earned it. Prop. 42 protects it.
CON
This is just another billionaire-funded trick. Prop. 42 isn’t really about protecting your retirement savings—its only real purpose is to undo the California Billionaire Tax. Billionaires would rather millions of Californians lose healthcare than pay a modest tax on their extreme wealth. Vote NO on 42.

# Proposition 42
Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes.
Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
## Analysis of Measure
### Background
Personal property is all the things that people own other than real estate.
...
### Proposal
***Prohibits New Taxes on Financial Assets or Other Personal Property.*** Under Proposition 42, new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property would not be allowed.
***Limits Retroactive Taxes.*** Proposition 42 limits the situations that a ballot measure or the Legislature can raise any tax retroactively.
A retroactive tax is one that applies to things that happened in the past.
An example is a tax on money someone earned two years ago.
...
## Yes/No Statement
A **YES** vote on this measure means: The state could not establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property.
A **NO** vote on this measure means: The state would continue to have the option to establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property.

# Proposition 42
Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes.
Initiative Constitutional Amendment.
## Analysis of Measure
### Proposal
***Prohibits New Taxes on Financial Assets or Other Personal Property.*** Under Proposition 42, new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property would not be allowed.
***Limits Retroactive Taxes.*** Proposition 42 limits the situations that a ballot measure or the Legislature can raise any tax retroactively.
A retroactive tax is one that applies to things that happened in the past.
An example is a tax on money someone earned two years ago.
#### Potential Interactions With Other Propositions
If Proposition 42 receives more “yes” votes than Proposition 40 on this same ballot, then Proposition 40 could be stopped from becoming law even if it gets yes votes from a majority of voters.

# Support slips for Prop 40 and Prop 45
The trendlines are troubling for Proposition 40, which would impose a one-time wealth tax on California’s billionaires, and for Proposition 45, which would streamline environmental reviews for construction projects.
Support for both measures has slipped markedly in the last month, according to the Public Policy Institute of California, as ballots hit mailboxes and millions of dollars in negative ads inundated the airwaves.
The wealth tax has seen an especially big swing: Support fell from 52% in September to 46% this month, while opposition rose from 46% to 52% — the first time a prominent public poll has found a majority of voters opposing the measure.
But Prop 45 also plunged underwater.
Opposition leads 50-46, reversing the measure’s 49-46 advantage in PPIC’s September poll.
...
Two billionaire-funded measures designed to torpedo Prop 40 were also on the bubble amid tightening polling: Proposition 41 declined from a 51-44 majority in September to 48-49 this month, and Proposition 42 went from 54-43 to 51-47.
Wealthy backers have largely focused on 42, pouring some $65 million into the campaign this month.
But the rest of the ballot is looking increasingly predictable as campaigns either held steady or saw polling gaps expand.

PROP
42
PROHIBITS NEW STATE PERSONAL PROPERTY TAXES AND CERTAIN RETROACTIVE STATE TAXES. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Prohibits any new state tax (1) imposed on the ownership of personal property (all things people own other than real estate), or (2) that applies retroactively based on taxpayer’s past activities. Nullifies taxes enacted after January 1, 2026 that conflict with this measure. Fiscal Impact: Possibility that tax revenues will not go up as much in the future. Supporters: CA Professional Firefighters; State Building & Construction Trades Council of CA; AMVETS Department of CA Opponents: US Senator Bernie Sanders; SEIU United Healthcare Workers West
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: The state could not establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: The state would continue to have the option to establish new taxes on the ownership of financial assets or other personal property.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
California’s Constitution currently allows the Legislature to tax retirement and savings—even though you already paid taxes on that money when you earned it! Prop. 42 protects Californians from this double taxation, by prohibiting new and retroactive taxes on personal property, including retirement and savings. You earned it. Prop. 42 protects it.
CON
This is just another billionaire-funded trick. Prop. 42 isn’t really about protecting your retirement savings—its only real purpose is to undo the California Billionaire Tax. Billionaires would rather millions of Californians lose healthcare than pay a modest tax on their extreme wealth. Vote NO on 42.

## Should California prohibit new taxes on financial assets like stocks and investment accounts and prohibit most retroactive taxes?
This would prohibit new taxes on financial assets — such as stocks — and other personal property.
It also prohibits most retroactive taxes.
Both of those provisions conflict with the wealth tax on billionaires proposed by Proposition 40, which seeks to tax financial assets and is retroactive to Jan. 1 of this year.
